key_insight: Quantile-based distributional reinforcement learning can estimate return distributions with optimal sample efficiency, achieving parametric √n rates and semiparametric efficiency for policy evaluation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a statistically grounded way to build reliable RL systems that estimate uncertainty in returns while supporting valid inference from finite samples.
method: Construct a finite-dimensional quantile-projected fixed point m for the return distribution.
Build an estimator m^(n) from an empirical MDP under a generative model.
Derive non-asymptotic W∞ error bounds, asymptotic normality, and Berry–Esseen guarantees for smooth functionals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports non-asymptotic error scaling of ~O(√(m/n)) and proves asymptotic efficiency, including matching semiparametric bounds in the infinite-quantile regime.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on access to a generative model and fixed-policy evaluation, so practical performance may depend on how well these assumptions match real RL data collection settings.
paper_title: Statistical Efficiency and Inference of Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
